definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese performing art in which dancers wear a lion-head mask and costume. Performed at festivals and New Year celebrations to ward off evil spirits and bring good luck. Having your head bitten by the lion is considered especially auspicious.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→お正月：05586_oshougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{獅子舞|ししまい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw a lion dance on New Year's.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{獅子舞|ししまい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{披露|ひろう}→披露：09683_hirou⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A lion dance was performed at the festival.

examples.japanese: {獅子舞|ししまい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧かまれる⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{無病|むびょう}{息災|そくさい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{過|す}ごせる→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It is said that having your head bitten by a lion dance brings health and safety from illness.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{獅子舞|ししまい} is one of Japan's most iconic traditional performing arts. The dancer wears a large, colorful lion head ({獅子頭|ししがしら}) and a long cloth body, often accompanied by musical instruments. It appears at New Year celebrations, shrine festivals, and local events throughout Japan.

A widely held belief is that being "bitten" on the head by the ⟦{獅子|しし}→獅子：04944_shishi⟧ (lion) brings good fortune and wards off illness, so children are often presented to the lion despite their tears.

Regional variations exist across Japan, from the two-person {獅子舞|ししまい} of the Kanto area to multi-person performances in other regions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {獅子舞|ししまい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{舞|ま}う→舞う：04573_mau⟧: to perform a lion dance
- {獅子舞|ししまい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧: to watch a lion dance
- {獅子舞|ししまい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧かまれる: to have one's head bitten by the lion
